newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia activists, youths detained at Timor meet.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia activists, youths detained at Timor meet.

text.p: Malaysian police detained about a dozen members of a Malaysian youth group and 30 local human rights activists on Saturday after the youths forcibly broke up a controversial meeting on East Timor.
A police official told reporters that Malaysian participants at the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor would be detained, but declined to say what the charges were.

"You've got to leave," the police official said when reporters asked him what charges, if any, were being brought against the activists, who tried to hold the East timor conference despite government objections.
Moments earlier, police took away about a dozen members of the Malaysian Action Front after they refused police demands to leave the conference venue.

The youth group, allied to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, broke up the meeting with boisterous chanting and singing of patriotic songs, saying the conference would damage Malaysia's ties with neighbouring Indonesia.

Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said this week the government would find legal ways to stop the conference. He said it could harm ties with neighbouring Indonesia, which invaded East Timor in December 1975 and annexed it the following year.
